transcript.text: I want to share my accounting classification finding with the committee now. While reviewing the bond terms this week, I determined that the contractual cash flows include a contingent step-up feature. Because of this feature, the position does not meet the SPPI test — the contractual cash flows are not solely payments of principal and interest on the principal amount outstanding. As a result, if we purchase these bonds, the position must be recorded at fair value through profit or loss rather than held at amortized cost. My accounting memo documenting this conclusion is prepared and awaiting circulation to the committee.

transcript.text: Thank you, Victor and Hassan. Let me now provide the full legal review for the committee. As I flagged earlier, I received a transfer-agent memo this afternoon with specific settlement requirements for this bond block. The key legal conditions are as follows: First, the bond block may settle only after the buyer — that would be us — provides a beneficial-owner certification. Second, the settlement must use an approved municipal-bond custodian. These are conditions precedent to settlement, meaning we cannot close this acquisition until both requirements are satisfied. From a legal standpoint, this affects both feasibility and timeline. We would need to confirm that our current custodial arrangements qualify under the approved municipal-bond custodian framework, and we would need to prepare and submit the beneficial-owner certification before settlement can occur. I should also note for the committee that I have not yet attached the transfer-agent memo to the trade file — I will do that promptly so it becomes part of the official committee record. Elena, with all four review areas now on the table — credit risk, legal, markets, and accounting — the committee is positioned to discuss whether to proceed and on what conditions.

transcript.text: Thank you, Nadia, for completing the legal review. With all four review areas now on the table, let me summarize the accounting position for the committee. The key takeaway from my review is that the contingent step-up feature in the bond terms means these bonds fail the SPPI test, so we cannot hold them at amortized cost — they must be recorded at fair value through profit or loss. This has two practical implications for the committee's decision. First, any mark-to-market gains or losses will flow directly through profit and loss each reporting period, which introduces earnings volatility that we would not have if the bonds qualified for amortized cost treatment. Second, at a purchase price of 82 cents on the dollar, the initial discount would not be accreted through interest income over the holding period as it would be under amortized cost — instead, the entire position is marked to fair value each period. My accounting memo is prepared and I will circulate it to the committee promptly so it becomes part of the official record. Elena, I believe the accounting review is now complete and on the table for the committee's consideration.
